### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4f9736fe7c761b125dceda0bb50612cf4bc7fc7b` — the merge of head `b6ae895c8baeef0c4c054e3374cdf4e5c6a07b14` into base `49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4f9736fe7c761b125dceda0bb50612cf4bc7fc7b && git checkout 4f9736fe7c761b125dceda0bb50612cf4bc7fc7b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439 b6ae895c8baeef0c4c054e3374cdf4e5c6a07b14 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439 && git merge --no-ff b6ae895c8baeef0c4c054e3374cdf4e5c6a07b14

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7a43945db5c334631fe1ee8d5703e03d3bf68c7f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/listed-row-changed-at.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-overlay-merge.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts

Read: card #36894 (body, the claim comment, the os-dev-report; no rulings, no earlier record), PR #36940 body and net diff against `main` at this head, and the 70 check-runs on this head (all `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed. The remainder (the two changed test files, the new test file, `authorable-surface/api.json`, `protocol.mdx`, the changeset prose, `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `GetMetaItemsResponseSchema.changedAt`, optional `record(string, string().datetime())` — right. Additive: the object is not strict, so a consumer on the old schema parses the new answer and a producer that omits the field still conforms. `datetime()` with no options accepts only the `Z` form, and the producer writes only `toISOString()` text (`storedRowChangedAt`), so every value produced parses.
- Accept-set of the producer: an item gets an entry only when the body the merge serves for its slot came from a stored `sys_metadata` row that recorded a readable `updated_at` (else `created_at`). A registry or MetadataService body gets none; a row with no time or an unparseable one gets none. Right, and it is the by-name read's rule (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:1173-1174`).
- Faces: only `audience === 'served' && layer === 'effective'` answers the field; the execution face and the per-package layer answer none, and the time is taken off every item on every face before return. Right.
- REST and runtime dispatcher: step 8a keeps only the keys whose name the answer still lists. Both transports reach it through `createMetaListAnswer` (`meta-collection-routes.ts:755`, `runtime/domains/meta.ts` `answerList`). Right for the keys; see S2 for the value.
- Other callers of `getMetaItems` (form routes, analytics, packages, automation, hono `/me/apps`, MCP `mcp-server-runtime.ts:815`, the stdio bridge) read `items` only and pass no sibling field on. Right.
- Generated surface: `api/GetMetaItemsResponse:changedAt` in `authorable-surface/api.json` and the `protocol.mdx` row match the schema line. `check:api-surface`, `check:docs`, `Spec property liveness` are green on the head.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`. The diff moves all three, and `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on each. Right. No major, no BREAKING banner owed: nothing is removed or tightened.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — accepted. The card fixes this kind and its acceptance says the changeset is levelled as a protocol addition; the claim, the PR body and the changeset agree; the repo's own ledger of the surface gained the key. Noted for the seat: AGENTS.md defines the kind by what an author can WRITE, and this key is response-only (the PR's own `Skills-docs` line says so). Read literally that is `none` plus a widening arm, which ships `patch`. `minor` is not below either reading, so no change is asked.
- `Clause-②: yes` — correct that the clause applies (a published response schema widens). The line carries no arm. The rule allows at most one arm, so the line is well-formed, and `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green. The precedent for the same position (`registrations`, d89f491) wrote `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. See N2.
- The line is the same in the claim, the PR body and the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations:

1. Surface beyond the claim's named files.
   - `protocol-overlay-merge.ts`, 3 lines plus one optional member on the records type — accepted. It is inside the claim's `packages/metadata-protocol/src/**` list-read clause, and it is the right place: the stamp is put on the contribution after `transform`, where the slot's content is chosen, so the time cannot be re-derived by name afterwards and land on another layer's body.
   - Step 8a in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` — accepted, and needed. The claim allows the REST door "only if it re-shapes the list envelope"; the chain drops items at steps 1, 2, 2a, 3, 4 and 7a, so an unpruned map would name items the caller is not listed. Residual: S2.
   - Row in `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` — accepted. It is the ledger row the gate requires for the new test's engine double; not a contract file, lane seat's remainder.
2. MCP `list_metadata_items` unchanged — accepted. It answers its own summary shape from `metaItemsArray(...)` and never carried `registrations` or `disabledActions`; nothing of the envelope reaches it.

Other dev flags: `test:repo` left to CI (`Test Core` 10/10 green on this head); suites run on the pre-merge head (the merge of `main` touched none of the three packages, and CI ran on this head); foreground CI wait. All answered, none escalated. `open_questions` is empty.

Out-of-scope note by the dev (the existing `registrations` and `disabledActions` pass the chain unpruned): read, agreed it is outside this PR; the same same-name question as S2 would apply to them if a gate ever drops a flow or an object.

SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Each time is read off a row the list already fetched (`readActiveOverlayRows`, the draft queries), and `storedOverlayEntries` over the stand-in and override rows was already called.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` against the card, the sibling precedent and the first consumer (#36898, a column keyed by item name, empty for code-shipped items):

- Position and key hold: beside `items`, keyed by `name`, the same identity `registrations` and `disabledActions` use and the console reads (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts`). The key carries no package and no bundle member; the schema says so and states the rule (the latest). For #36898 this means every row of one name shows one time; acceptable for a column, declared, and noted for that card.
- The three readings the dev asked to be checked, each read in the tree:
  - Effective layer on the list naming no package: holds. `mergePackageAwareOverlay` picks one contribution per (slot, package) through `servedStoredRow`, and the time is on that contribution's own copy. A slot the registry wins is served from a base item, which has none. A newer row of another layer cannot win the time without winning the content. Pinned in both row orders on both lists.
  - Draft row time on `?preview=draft`: holds. The draft merge takes the first merge's output as base (times kept by spread) and stamps each draft from its own row; where a draft wins the slot its time is served, otherwise the active row's.
  - Two rows of one name, the latest wins: holds (`listedChangedAt`, compared as instants, not as text).
- `storedEntryChangedAt` pairs rows to entries by index: `storedOverlayEntries` is a one-to-one, in-order `map` (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts:157`), and a length mismatch pairs nothing. Holds.
- Break attempt, a key for an item the answer does not list: none found. In the protocol the map is built in the governed loop, after every drop (`unseated`, `names`, the moved-edit filter, disabled packages, action withholding, view containers), and that loop drops nothing. In the REST chain 8a runs after every dropping step; step 9 translates and drops nothing; the early returns of 7 and 7a answer a fault with no data.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — `app` list: an app served from a stored row loses its entry when any package contributes nav to it. `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts:1015` maps every app through `registry.applyNavContributions` before the take-off loop, and that function returns `structuredClone(app)` when the app has contributions (`packages/objectql/src/registry-apps.ts:142`). `structuredClone` copies own enumerable string keys only, so the symbol-keyed time is gone and `takeListedRowChangedAt` finds none. The schema says "One entry per listed item served from a stored row" and that the time is the instant the by-name read serves as `Last-Modified`; the by-name read still serves it for the same app, so the two doors disagree. Card acceptance ("change an item in a self-built package and the list carries its time") fails for such an app. No test lists an `app`. Fix direction: take the time before this step, or re-stamp after it, and pin it.

S2 (should-fix) — the time of a withheld item can still be served under a name the caller is listed. The protocol folds every same-name item into one value (the latest) before the per-caller gate runs, and step 8a prunes by name only. Construction: packages A and B both ship dashboard `d` (both listed on the list naming no package, ADR-0048); A's is served from a stored row and carries `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks, B's is code-shipped. The gate drops A's item and keeps B's, `d` is still listed, so `changedAt.d` is A's row time. The answer then gives a time to an item that has no stored row, and discloses when the withheld item changed. This breaks the schema sentence "Where several listed items share a name, the latest of their times" (the time is of an item not listed) and the PR's own claim that a withheld item's change time is not disclosed. The same holds for the other per-item drops (step 1, the view gate, step 4, step 7a). Small in reach (needs one name in two packages with one withheld), but it is the guarantee 8a was added for. Fix direction: drop the entry of any name the chain removed an item of, or carry the per-item time to the gate and fold after it.

Nits (no change asked on this head):

- N1 — a view expanded from a stored aggregated container row gets no entry, though its content came from a stored row. This matches the by-name read (no row of the item's own name is adopted), but the schema description only contrasts "stored row" with "code". One clause in the description would say it. Follow-up or accepted deviation.
- N2 — `Clause-②: yes` has no `(widening)` arm, where the `registrations` precedent wrote one. Well-formed and green; accepted deviation.
- N3 — the helper's module doc says the row time "is taken off each item ... on every face", which is true, and that an object spread carries it through "every copy"; S1 is the one copy that is not a spread. Fix the sentence with S1.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence: `listed-row-changed-at.ts`, `protocol-overlay-merge.ts` and the stamping and take-off hunks of `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` agree with the schema text except where S1 says; `meta-item-read-gate.ts` step 8a agrees with "Only the names of items in this answer are keyed" and falls short of the value rule as S2 says.

S1 and S2 are open on this head; each earns a delta review of its fix. Nothing found here is graded above them.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv4KRPATgwPAzKKMU`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 7a43945d · 2026-11-24T10:50Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `7a43945db5c334631fe1ee8d5703e03d3bf68c7f`
Reviewer: L1-b (seat 3, area ux-E2). Contract review: L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head, comment 7129296586 (claim 7129140379). Its verdict is PASS, with two should-fix findings open, each owing a delta review.
Tier: not Tier H. This is card #36894's only PR, 12 files, 608 changed lines. `check-governed-merges --pr 36940`: not governed.

### Read
- Net diff `origin/main...7a43945d`, the PR body, card #36894 with claim 7126810309 and dev report 7129039206.
- Check-runs on `7a43945d`: 60 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `l1-face.mjs --pr 36940`: CLEAN, 13 items, none flagged.

### Checklist
- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36894`, plus `Part of #36890`.
- **Scope.** The spec schema and its generated `api.json` and `protocol.mdx`; `listed-row-changed-at.ts` (new); `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`; the three lines in `protocol-overlay-merge.ts`; step 8a in `meta-item-read-gate.ts`; tests; the engine-double ledger row; and the changeset. The three declared deviations are each needed, and the L2 accepts them. MCP `list_metadata_items` reads `items` only and is correctly left alone.
- **Design.** The time is carried on an enumerable symbol stamped where the merge chooses each slot's content. It is taken off every item where the list assembles its answer, and is answered only on the served effective list. This is sound, and the three readings the dev asked about hold: the effective layer on `~all`, the draft row time on `?preview=draft`, and the latest of one name. I re-read S1 myself: `applyNavContributions` (`registry-apps.ts:142`) returns `structuredClone(app)` when the app has contributions, and `structuredClone` does not copy symbol-keyed members.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/rest` minor, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. The level matches the card.
- **Card acceptance.**
  - The list carries the time of an item changed in a self-built package: met for most types, not met for an `app` with nav contributions (S1).
  - A code-shipped item carries none: not guaranteed when one name is held by a code item and a withheld stored item (S2).
  - The layer rule on `~all` is tested: met.
  - `check:api-surface`, `check:docs` and the list type pins pass: met.

### Findings
- **S1 (should-fix), adopted from the L2 record.** An `app` served from a stored row loses its `changedAt` entry when any package contributes nav to it. `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts:1015` maps every app through `registry.applyNavContributions`, which returns a `structuredClone` that drops the symbol-keyed time, before the take-off loop. The by-name read still serves `Last-Modified` for the same app, so the two doors disagree. The Setup app is built from contributions, so this is not rare. To fix, take the time before that step, or re-stamp after it, and add a pin that lists an `app` with a contribution.
- **S2 (should-fix), adopted from the L2 record.** The protocol folds same-name items into one time before the per-caller gate. Step 8a then prunes by name only, so a withheld item's time can be served under a name that is still listed. Example: A's stored dashboard `d` is withheld, and B's code-shipped `d` stays listed. The answer then gives a time to an item that has no stored row, and tells the caller when the withheld item changed. To fix, drop the entry of any name the chain removed an item of, or carry each item's time to the gate and fold after it. Add a pin for the two-package case.
- The L2 record's N1–N3 are adopted as nits. N3 (the helper's module doc says the time survives every copy) is best fixed together with S1.

### Delta
The fix moves the head, so it owes a delta L1 and a delta L2 on the new head. Send the new head to L1-b.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6ae895c8baeef0c4c054e3374cdf4e5c6a07b14`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/listed-row-changed-at.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts

Delta review of record 7129296586 (head `7a43945d`), which left S1 and S2 open. Read: the delta `7a43945d..b6ae895c` (four commits, no merge from `main`, 8 files, +124/-35), the round-2 os-dev-report 7130215825, the updated PR body, and the check-runs on this head. `protocol-overlay-merge.ts` did not move this round; the earlier record's reading of it stands. The remainder (the two test files, `protocol.mdx`, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

S1: closed
S2: closed

### ① Derived judgments

- Schema shape unchanged: `changedAt` is still the optional `record(string, string().datetime())`. Only its description moved. Right.
- Accept-set of the REST and runtime chain narrows: an entry is now kept only for a name of which the chain's answer lists at least as many items as the store's answer did, and at least one. An entry is dropped, never recomputed. Right, and it is the conservative direction: the field under-reports, it never reports another item's time.
- Accept-set of the protocol list widens by the S1 case only: a stored-row `app` that has nav contributions now keeps its entry. Right.
- Generated reference: the `protocol.mdx` row equals the new description text.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `minor` on the three moved packages under `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes`. The declaration lines did not move in the changeset or the PR body; only one prose bullet of the changeset changed, and it matches the tree. The notes of the earlier record on the kind and the missing `(widening)` arm stand as accepted, no change asked.

### ③ Boundary flags

Round-2 dev deviations:

- PR body not edited by the dev (the seat owns it) — answered: the body on this head now describes step 8a as dropping a name the chain removed an item of, and has the nav-fold paragraph. One stale line remains in its ablation fold ("REST step 8a removed: 2 failed / 16 passed", a round-1 count); prose only, see N4.
- overlap-check run once after the pushes, clean — accepted.

`open_questions`: none. SQL push-down: no finding; the delta adds no query, id materialisation or in-app join (step 8a counts names over two lists already in memory).

Check-runs on this head: 61 `success`, 12 `skipped`, none failed. One `Check Changeset` run, started 11:33:20Z after the PR-body edit, was still `in_progress` when read; the earlier `Check Changeset` run on this same head is `success`, and the changeset's declaration lines did not change. The seat confirms that run ends green before the record is used.

### ④ Design judgment

The four checks asked for this round:

1. S2, does the detection see every dropping step, and how is "removed" computed. It is computed by count, not by tracking names through steps: `itemCountsByName` over the store's answer (`raw`, the chain's untouched input) and over the list as it stands at 8a, per `name`; an entry survives only where `after >= before` and `after > 0`. Because it compares the chain's input with its state at 8a, it does not depend on which step dropped: step 1 (the `api` served set), the per-caller gate of every type, `?names`, `?id`, `?object`, and step 7a are all covered, and so is any step added above 8a later. Steps 5, 6, 7 and 8 map items and keep `name`; steps 7 and 7a answer a fault with no data on their early return; step 9 translates and drops nothing. Both transports hand the store's answer in as `raw` (`meta-collection-routes.ts`, `runtime/domains/meta.ts` `answerMetaList`).
   Removed and then re-added by another path: a count cannot tell a swap from no change, so it would slip only if a step above 8a ADDED an item of a name. None does: every step is a filter or a one-to-one map over the list it was given, and step 1 answers a selection of the stored items. Holds on this tree. Stated as N5 so the invariant is not lost.
2. S1, is the re-stamp keyed correctly. It is not keyed at all: inside one `map` callback the time is taken off an app, the fold runs on that same app, and the time is put back on that fold's own result. Two apps of one name in two packages are two callbacks, so one app's time cannot land on another. `withListedRowChangedAt` spreads the clone, so the fold's result is not written. An app with no contributions comes back as itself and is re-stamped the same way. The take-off in the governed loop still strips it from every returned item.
3. Schema description and changeset against the tree. The new sentence "a door that leaves out some item of a name ... answers no entry for that name" is what step 8a does. "A view a stored view container expands ... has no entry" is what the list does (an expansion body carries no time) and folds the earlier N1 in. The changeset bullet says the same as the schema. The helper's module doc now says only spread copies carry the time and names the nav fold (earlier N3, done). All match.
4. New findings: none graded. Tried: a name whose only listed item is code-shipped (no entry in the store's map, nothing to keep); a name with a non-string or missing `name` (not counted on either side, cannot be a key); an array-shaped answer (no sibling field, returned as is); a partial drop where the remaining item is the stored one (entry dropped, an under-report the schema now states). The two pins (section 6 for S1; the two-package `d` case with a permitted-caller control for S2) assert the behaviour read here.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (no change asked on this head):

- N4 — the PR body's ablation fold still carries a round-1 count for step 8a. Prose face; the seat may fix it without moving the head.
- N5 — step 8a's count rule relies on no step above it adding an item. One sentence in the step list of `createMetaListAnswer` would say so. Follow-up or accepted deviation.
